findings.message: deploy_agent_run calls `deploy_release_run` with no arguments, but plugins/tool/deploy-release/plugin.sh:21-34 requires `state_file` as `$2` and returns rc=1 (writing `disposition=broken`) when that argument is empty — every non-dry-run deploy with a passing gate will fail at this guard; tests pass only because they mock `deploy_release_run` via `_ZBUILD_DEPLOY_RELEASE_LOADED=1` and the mock accepts any arity.

The deploy agent catches any non-zero rc from `deploy_release_run` and unconditionally writes `disposition=unavailable`, overwriting the deploy-release plugin's own result (which distinguishes `broken` for a local git-tag collision from `unavailable` for a network push failure); the engine's retry policy will re-attempt permanently-broken deploys — an outward-facing action against a live repo — when it should block.

`deploy_agent_run` returns rc=1 without writing any result file or summary when `ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR` is unset; the manifest declares `deploy-result.json` as `required:true primary:true`, so the engine detects the absence via the fail-closed scanner but an operator has no diagnostic artifact and no structured disposition to distinguish this from a deploy-content failure.

deploy-release still derives its own `artifacts_dir` from `state_file` (v1 pattern) and writes `deploy-result.json` to that path; if the calling-convention gap in finding #1 were fixed, the deploy-release result would land in a state-file-derived path while the deploy agent's success-path call to `_deploy_write_result` writes to `ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR` — the engine only scans the latter, so deploy-release's output would be orphaned; this pre-existed this change.
